source_text: Si ergo nec calamitas nec imbecillitas nec libido ei praevaricationis incumbit, qui fieri potest, ut eam iustitiae formam, quam commendavit iubendo, destruat iudicando, immo non in istam iustitiam, sed in reverentiam suam saeviat (tanta est quippe aequitatis potentia, ut et deviantes arguat et nulla fugientium a se auctoritate minuatur) postremo ut quae sunt iusta a nobis fieri velit et ipse faciat quod iniustum est? Iustiores nos, quam ipse est, cupit videri, immo non iustiores, sed nos aequos et se iniquum?
pass_a_gloss: If therefore neither calamity nor weakness nor desire of transgression lies upon him, how can it happen that he destroy by judging that form of justice which he commended by commanding, nay rather rage not against that justice but against reverence of himself (for so great is the power of fairness that it both argues those who deviate and is diminished by no authority of those fleeing from it), finally that he want those things which are just to be done by us and himself do what is unjust? Does he desire us to seem more just than he himself is, nay not more just, but us fair and himself unjust?

lemmas.lexica: LS libido; Blaise often sexual desire; Julian treats as created sensation, not a sin-nature

pass_b_english: If neither calamity nor weakness nor a desire to transgress bears on him, how can he destroy in judging the pattern of justice he commended by commanding? Indeed, he would be raging not against that justice but against reverence for himself. For fairness has such power that it both condemns those who stray and loses none of its force through the authority of those who abandon it. How, finally, could he want us to do what is just and himself do what is unjust? Does he want us to seem more just than he is—or rather, not more just, but ourselves fair and himself unfair?

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
